rows.sourceExpression: the ground shifting under their feet
rows.sourceExample: Workers felt the ground shifting under their feet as the industry changed.
rows.sourceMeaning: Basic conditions changing in an unsettling way; a fixed ground metaphor.
rows.decisionReason: Workers feeling “the ground shifting under their feet” as an industry changes uses the same destabilised-familiar-conditions metaphor as canonical 2026 “the ground is shifting under their feet”. The source omits the copula under felt, a grammatical frame rather than a distinct meaning. The owner now teaches both natural forms, contains a new transfer context and retains exact source provenance.

rows.sourceExample: She passes those stories on to her children.
rows.sourceMeaning: Transmits stories to another generation; a natural phrasal verb.
rows.decisionReason: The source “passes those stories on to her children” uses the same transmission phrasal verb as canonical 1326 “pass on values / experience and tradition”. Stories are the transmitted object; separable object placement is already part of that verb’s grammar, not a distinct sense. The owner now includes stories and exact source provenance.

rows.sourceExample: The festival has deep roots here.
rows.sourceMeaning: A long-established cultural connection; a plant metaphor.
rows.decisionReason: The festival having “deep roots here” is the same long-established connection metaphor as canonical 1471 “deep roots in family life”; here identifies a local place rather than family life, not a separate image or outcome. The owner now teaches both contexts and records exact source provenance.
